summary: In this excerpt from Book 6, the narrator pleads with Checker to drop an investigation into the narrator's memory loss, saying it is their own life and they want the past kept locked away. Checker refuses, citing possible danger and enemies, and the narrator leaves the Hole without looking back. After a night of nightmares, the narrator goes out into the darkened streets seeking strong chemical remedies.
one_line: The narrator begs Checker to abandon an investigation into their damaged memory, is refused, storms out, and turns to drugs.
key_facts: The narrator tells Checker, "I don't need a reason," and asks him to "Leave it alone. Please."
Checker says "I can't" when asked to let the matter go, insisting the narrator might be in danger.
Checker argues that whatever happened to the narrator might be influencing them to ask him to stop investigating.
The narrator says, "If you're in trouble, I'll come," and says Checker should call when he changes his mind.
The narrator pushes open the door and leaves the Hole without looking back.
Checker calls after the narrator, imploring and frantic, but the narrator does not acknowledge him.
The narrator dreams of "half-real monsters" who smother them in false memory and distorted realities.
The narrator wakes a few hours later and stumbles toward the darkened streets.
The narrator seeks "the strongest chemical remedies money and back alleyways could offer."
The narrator describes their brain as "broken, already-damaged" and wants to keep it all locked away.
Checker speaks slowly and quietly, his voice cracking, and holds the narrator's eyes pleadingly.
The narrator says, "Cas, don't make me—" in the exchange, indicating Cas is the narrator's name as used by Checker.

entities.name: Checker
entities.role: Character who refuses to drop the investigation into the narrator's memory and pleads with the narrator as they leave

entities.name: Cas
entities.role: Name Checker uses to address the narrator (the first-person speaker)

entities.name: the Hole
entities.role: Location the narrator leaves after the confrontation with Checker
